questions.title: Which Indian state will have the highest reported death toll from monsoon floods and landslides as of August 5, 2026?
questions.background: India's annual monsoon can cause fatal floods and landslides across multiple states.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Indian state with the highest reported cumulative death toll from monsoon floods and landslides since July 1, 2026, according to official data cited in news reporting Resolution Date : August 5, 2026 Accepted Answer Format : The state's name
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-20 empirical and IMD update (Millennium Post July 21 01:16 IST, The Hindu July 21 04:12 IST, The Watchers/IMD 13:40 IST bulletin, Reuters/Al Jazeera, HinduBusinessLine): (1) Jammu and Kashmir jumps sharply (0.09 -> 0.14, overtaking UP for #4): toll climbed to 23 confirmed dead in 48 hours (11 more Monday in Poonch/Rajouri/Doda) with 7 still missing and IMD forecasting heavy-to-extremely-heavy rain for 3+ more days—bringing J&K's effective toll right alongside Maharashtra's early-July bank (~25-35+), though still discounted ~45-48% for Union Territory vs constitutional state resolution risk (note TechTimes/HinduBusinessLine/Millennium Post grouped J&K with states while Scroll.in labeled it a UT). (2) Himachal Pradesh drops (0.26 -> 0.21, falling to #2): Day 1 of its July 20 Red Alert passed with zero reported fatalities and SEOC road closures declining from 70 to 36, though a 5-district Red Alert for July 21 (Chamba, Kangra, Kullu, Mandi, Sirmaur) and active monsoon through July 25 keep strong upside through Aug 5. (3) Maharashtra holds 0.24 (retaking #1): maintains the largest confirmed banked post-July-1 toll among the 28 constitutional states while HinduBusinessLine/IMD notes continued widespread rain over Konkan/Goa and heavy showers over Madhya Maharashtra this week. (4) Uttarakhand rises slightly (0.15 -> 0.16): landslide-blocked roads nearly doubled to ~150 (including 4 national highways), Char Dham Yatra was suspended, 220 mm extreme rain fell at Shama, statewide schools closed, and a child was swept away in Bageshwar on July 20. (5) Uttar Pradesh holds 0.11 after IMD upgraded parts of UP to a Red Alert for extremely heavy rain over the next 24h plus rain through July 24. Residual 14% tail reflects Assam's sharp July 20 escalation (3.63 lakh affected across 16 districts—6x Sunday's figure—5 dead in 48h, 370 mm in Meghalaya hills, Army/IAF standby), Bihar (200 mm at Siwan), Gujarat (~17 banked), Nagaland (9 dead in Mon), and other states.

questions.title: Who will score India's first half-century in the July 2026 Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe?
questions.background: A half-century in cricket is an individual score of at least 50 runs in one innings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the first Indian batter to reach 50 runs in an innings during the July 2026 men's Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe, according to official match scorecards and contemporaneous match reports. Resolution Date : 2026-07-23 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the batter's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major July 7-14 batting form and lineup update ahead of the July 23 Zimbabwe T20I series (Hindustan Times July 12-14, Khaleej Times July 12-13): BCCI's July 12 squad revision replaced only injured bowler Varun Chakaravarthy with Ravi Bishnoi, leaving the Zimbabwe batting squad intact. However, India lost 0-4 to England and 0-2 to Ireland, and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi failed in all three England T20Is (42 runs across 3 innings, never crossing 20) before being DROPPED for the 5th T20I in Southampton. July 13-14 reporting notes 'it remains to be seen whether he gets any game time' in Zimbabwe, with maiden call-up right-handed opener Prabhsimran Singh (or promoted WK opener Ishan Kishan) creating ~50-55% risk that Sooryavanshi is benched for the 1st T20I in Harare (when India's first 50 is most likely scored). Cutting Sooryavanshi sharply 0.17 -> 0.11 (#4), elevating captain Shreyas Iyer 0.13 -> 0.16 (#3, cited by HT July 12 as the only Indian batter who looked accomplished in England and guaranteed #3/#4 starter), boosting locked-in opener Abhishek Sharma 0.26 -> 0.28 (prior Harare T20I centurion) and guaranteed top-3 starter Ishan Kishan 0.21 -> 0.23 (world #1 T20I batter, could also open), and holding vice-captain Tilak Varma at 0.10 (guaranteed #4/#5 starter with improved 5th T20I form), leaving 12% residual led by Prabhsimran Singh (~8%), Shivam Dube (~2%), and Rinku Singh (~1.5%).

questions.title: Which European country will declare a national emergency in response to wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements or reliable news reporting published by July 25, 2026. Resolution Condition : Identify the European country whose national government declares a national emergency because of wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026. Regional or local emergency declarations alone do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20 escalation in Spain (Reuters July 20, AnewZ/Reuters July 18, AFP July 20): no European national wildfire emergency has been declared yet through July 20, but Spain's La Mierla blaze in Guadalajara more than doubled again in 24 hours from >12,000 ha on July 19 to over 26,000 ha on Monday July 20—becoming Spain's largest fire of 2026—forcing three additional municipality evacuations (>1,000 evacuated) with regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page warning nearly 30 population centres are surrounded. Alongside the >15,400 ha Aragon/Zaragoza fire (crossing toward Navarre under Level 2 emergency with UME deployed), EU Copernicus shows Spain at 104,423 ha burned YTD (2.5x France's 41,781 ha), and AEMET warns a new 42-44C heatwave with dry thunderstorms will last through Thursday July 23 right ahead of Tuesday's July 21 Council of Ministers. Lifting Spain sharply 0.34 -> 0.45 (still capped below 0.50 given Madrid's historical reluctance to invoke central Nivel 3 over autonomous regions), trimming Portugal (0.24 -> 0.20, same Iberian heatwave), Greece (0.12 -> 0.10), and North Macedonia (0.10 -> 0.09), and holding Italy at 0.03 (13% residual for Bulgaria, Cyprus, Albania, Croatia, Montenegro, Turkey, and France where July 19's 200-ha Var blaze was reported favourable).
